statements.t: “We finished the third quarter with strong execution against our operational and financial targets while also advancing our large customer strategy that we expect will continue to drive affordability benefits for our customers.

“We are also pleased to announce the signing of three amendments to previously signed electric service agreements that, in total, are expected to drive ~250 megawatts of incremental load, further augmenting the affordability benefits for our customers as provided by the large load power service tariff.

“Given results ahead of expectations driven by strong operational performance and warmer weather, we are increasing our 2026 adjusted EPS guidance range to $4.35 to $4.50 per share from $4.14 to $4.34 per share.
We increased our dividend by 4%, which supports our long-term payout ratio target range of 50% to 60%.

We are also reaffirming our long-term adjusted EPS annual growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030 off the original 2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint of $4.24, with the expectation that annual EPS growth will exceed 8% beginning in 2028 and through 2030.”
The Company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) guidance range to $4.35 to $4.50 from its original guidance range of $4.14 to $4.34.

Additionally, the Company reaffirmed its long-term adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) annual growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030 based on the original 2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) guidance midpoint of $4.24.
The Company expects annual adjusted EPS growth to exceed 8% beginning in 2028 and through 2030.
Evergy management is not able to forecast if any of these items will occur or any amounts that may be reported for future periods.

Management also makes assumptions regarding the run rate of operations, maintenance and general and administrative costs based on the expected outcome of the aforementioned events.
This capital expenditure forecast is subject to management's discretion and continual review and could change.
